_why: Suggested starting values for the settlement setup page. They live here, not in source, for two reasons: npm run verify fails the build if an address or endpoint appears in src/ or scripts/, and a value without its provenance is a value nobody can re-check. Every entry names where it came from and when it was confirmed.

X402_FACILITATOR_URL.source: Free community testnet facilitator. Confirmed live: GET /supported returned x402Version 2, scheme exact, network eip155:84532. No API key.

X402_NETWORK.source: Base Sepolia in CAIP-2. Listed by the facilitator's /supported. The server re-checks this at startup rather than trusting it.

X402_ASSET.source: USDC on Base Sepolia, as it appears in the x402 v2 specification's own examples (specs/x402-specification-v2.md). Verify against Circle before a mainnet run.

X402_ASSET_NAME.source: EIP-712 domain name, needed to reconstruct the signed transferWithAuthorization message.

X402_ASSET_VERSION.source: EIP-712 domain version, from the same specification example.

X402_ATOMIC_PER_UNIT.source: How many atomic token units one unit of a quoted price is worth. USDC has 6 decimals, so 1 means a 120 JPYC request settles as 0.000120 USDC. Demo scale, chosen so a faucet wallet survives a booth.

X402_EXPLORER_URL.source: Where a settled transaction can be looked at without going through us.

faucet.source: Circle's testnet USDC faucet. The buyer wallet needs USDC and no ETH, because the facilitator pays gas.
